question: Which country grows about nine-tenths of the world's saffron?
answer: Iran, about 90% of a world harvest of roughly 300 tonnes, much of it from Khorasan, where some fields are still watered by qanats, underground channels centuries old. Spain, whose name sells saffron at a premium, grows very little and has long exported far more than it harvests, repacking imported threads.
move: Ask where a product is grown, not where it was last packed.
trap: La Mancha labels are the famous ones, so Spain seems the source.
source: FAO in Iran, saffron value chain
